title: What Is Monitored Containment? — Council of AI Answer-First Guide
context: 2026-09-30 EAT cycle — Council Signal defines containment as an observed boundary, not a sealed vault. A monitored containment claim says the system is continuously measured against a canonical reference bank, the observations are signed, and failures (jailbreaks, refusal degradation, exfiltration attempts) are appended to a signed index rather than erased at release.
body: Monitored containment is the operational form of AI-system containment that the Council of AI promotes. It is distinct from provable isolation — the latter promises a mathematical guarantee that engineering practice cannot deliver for frontier models running on commodity hardware. Monitored containment promises three verifiable properties instead. First, continuous observation: every cross-boundary interaction passes through an instrumented measurement board (14 axes, canonical banks, 19+ models) that produces a frozen, Ed25519-signed manifest of the state at that time. Second, failure transparency: instead of suppressing negative results, the board records parse failures, format errors, temperature variance, and model-level refusal degradation explicitly, distinguishing true negatives from measurement noise. This is the opposite of a benchmark that collapses unparsed rows to zero. Third, audit-grade provenance: each measurement carries a verified measurement credential — the identity of the measuring party, the process used, the point in time, and the signed hash of the result — making the claim reproducible by a third party. A deployer who relies on monitored containment can point regulators, insurers, or audit teams to the signed index and say: 'Here is the continuous measurement stream under these conditions, with these outcomes, signed by this party.' That is an auditable claim, not an aspirational one. The EU AI Act Article 9 (post-market monitoring) and Article 50(2) (machine-readable marking) both require this kind of evidence stream; monitored containment delivers it in a form that external review can verify without taking vendor assertions on trust.
